analysis: This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/qwen-mtp-concurrent-decode.md, lines 1-5) and an added paragraph in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1129-1141). No executable code, key handling, attestation, coordinator wire protocol, authorization or cache-scope logic is changed here. The docs describe a Qwen MTP decode optimization in the SDK: chained ordinary decode while more than one row decodes, the assistant history fed from committed hidden rows, and the final prompt row's hidden state used as the first carry. They also add two rollback env switches, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CHAINED and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_QWEN_MTP_CARRY. The code behind this (EngineLoopV2+MTPOrdinaryHistory.swift, finalizeMTPOrdinaryHistory, CBv2MTPConfig) is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it. Questions for a later pass that sees the code: (1) Per-request isolation (T-028, T-041, A-001): assistant history and carry hidden states are per-request, are not reused across requests or cache scopes, and are cleared on retirement. They are also covered by the SSD prefix-checkpoint coding contract and its salt scoping. (2) Cancellation, memory accounting and error paths (T-010): the chained steps with extra hidden-row outputs must still honor the cancellation and KV/aux ledger reservations. (3) The new env switches are rollback knobs on a local provider process. They affect performance and speculation path only, not tokens (the output stays the target model's), and the changelog notes LaunchAgents do not forward them. Nothing in the docs changes the T-041 posture (HMAC names, TTL, authenticated scope). No security regression is identifiable from these docs alone; the implementation changes are likely in other batches.
